brief: US forces resumed strikes in Iran after about a one-month pause and, on Friday, announced a takeover of Venezuela oil reserves. Despite this, oil options markets show no bid for upside tails: call premium is fading and low-delta puts trade higher than their levels last Thursday, before the Venezuela announcement. The 25-delta 1-month risk reversal, which measures call premium over puts of similar tenor and moneyness, sits near the bottom of its recent range, underperforming the bounce in flat price. Strait of Hormuz crossings have been contracting, with reports of 2-4 million barrels/day versus the US administration's claim of 8-10 million b/d, yet markets remain hesitant to lean either way, producing a tame reaction to the renewed strikes. The author attributes this to a "U-turn decay dynamic": repeated US-Iran course changes have made oil headlines generate progressively smaller market reactions over time. Markets read the strikes as posturing rather than a meaningful escalation in physical disruption risk. As oil risk shifts from cracks back to flat price and systematic upside-price levels are potentially hit, this complacency could fade quickly once the Brent futures roll window passes this week.
